clue.text: Live it up out with noted parent

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the following words are to be rearranged

blocks.note: the three words supply the letters for rearranging, fifteen in all

explanation.surface: A wild night out with a parent who is a well-known figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out celebrating extravagantly, which is exactly living it up.

clue.text: Delivering rebuff, carrying on without emotion

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of another, so these pieces are stacked one after the other

blocks.note: a cold person shows no feeling
shouldering a load is carrying it

explanation.surface: Someone bearing a burden calmly while snubbing another person.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the second piece is placed on top of the first, so the 'without emotion' word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the cold shoulder is the idiom for snubbing or deliberately ignoring them, a deliberate rebuff.

clue.text: It shows the bigger picture

blocks.note: surface reading: something that gives an overview of a situation
setter's reading: a literally larger, wider image on a television or cinema display

explanation.walkthrough: 'The bigger picture' is an idiom for the overall view, but here it is meant literally: a wide display format.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-format display, as in cinemas or modern televisions, presents a broader image than the old square format.

clue.text: Slippery character handed over cash without hesitation

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: money handed over has been spent
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A shifty person paid out money without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but 'without' means outside: the paid-out word wraps the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is literally slippery, and the word is also used figuratively for a treacherous, sly person.

clue.text: Drive off, cutting short filming

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its tail, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a film shoot is a session of filming

explanation.surface: A film crew is chased away, ending the day's filming early.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the word called out to scare away an animal or person, so it means to chase off.

clue.text: Get cross having to rush away before the opener

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next in the finished word

blocks.note: to fly off is to leave in a hurry
taken as written
a door handle is what you use to open a door

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at having to leave before the opening act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opener' suggests a first act or a bottle opener; here it is the thing you turn to open a door.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose your temper suddenly, so it is a colourful way of becoming angry.

clue.text: Might a Tory often upset official delegation?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: might as a noun means strength
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Conservative frequently annoys a formal delegation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb opening a question; it is the noun meaning strength. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal document formally authorises one person to act on another's behalf, an official handing over of authority.

clue.text: Plant is no distance from river

blocks.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
O looks like zero, nothing
a mile is a unit of distance

explanation.surface: A plant growing right beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No distance from' reads as 'right next to', but 'no' and 'distance' each give letters, placed after the river.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a daisy-like herb, familiar as the flowers used to make a soothing tea.

clue.text: Keep going for Just a Minute

blocks.note: first meaning: persist, carry on despite difficulty
second meaning: a request to wait briefly

explanation.walkthrough: Just a Minute is a BBC radio panel game in which players must talk without pausing, so the capitals make it look like one idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to persist through hardship and, as an exclamation, to ask someone to wait a moment.

clue.text: Nervous of operating something sharp

blocks.note: a machine that is operating is on
the edge of a blade is its sharp part

explanation.surface: Feeling anxious about using a sharp tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being tense, anxious and easily startled.

clue.text: In favour of parent ditching husband for impresario

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of, so a letter is removed from the word it follows

blocks.note: pro means for or in favour of
a mother is a parent
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Supporting a parent who abandons her husband for a showbusiness producer.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances concerts or shows, the same role as one who stages and publicises events.

clue.text: Craving starters in the curry house

indicators.note: starters are the opening parts of something, here the initial letter of each following word

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Hunger for the appetisers at an Indian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' plays on the restaurant course; here it means the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch for something is a restless longing or desire, a figurative use of the skin sensation.

clue.text: It's always diverting

blocks.note: surface reading: something endlessly entertaining or amusing
setter's reading: redirecting traffic onto the opposite side of a road during works

explanation.walkthrough: 'Diverting' suggests amusing, but it means sending traffic another way. This is a British roadworks arrangement where vehicles share the other carriageway of a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrangement exists to send vehicles away from their usual lane, so its whole purpose is redirecting traffic.

clue.text: It won't flourish without support

blocks.note: surface reading: a person or venture that needs backing to succeed
setter's reading: a climbing vegetable that must be trained up canes or poles

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a needy person or business; the support is a literal cane for a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing vegetable twines upward and must be given tall canes or strings to grow well.

clue.text: Perplexed to get the sack when full of inspiration

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: sack is slang for bed, as in hitting the sack
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: Someone baffled at being fired despite brimming with ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the sack' looks like being dismissed from a job; the sack is slang for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means puzzled or bewildered, so it is a direct synonym for perplexed.

clue.text: Half missed moment Hal without king makes entrance

indicators.note: half of the word is missing, so only its second half survives
without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its front half
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Prince Hal arrives on stage at a moment when the king is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun for coming in; it is the verb meaning to delight, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral someone is to captivate and hold their attention completely, the verb sense of entrance.

clue.text: Master wrestling holds in advance

indicators.note: a thing that holds another keeps it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling
pre is the prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: An expert wrestler grips an opponent before the bout begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, a boss or leader, which matches master in the sense of chief.

clue.text: Guiding principle of Midas's reign?

blocks.note: surface reading: a basic rule of conduct
setter's reading: the period of government by the mythical king whose touch turned everything to gold

explanation.walkthrough: King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so his rule would literally be gilded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the ethic of treating others as you wish to be treated, or any fundamental rule.

clue.text: Resent some that escaped

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the answer is a run of letters inside the following words

blocks.note: a run spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Bearing a grudge against those who got away.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent someone is to feel bitter ill will toward them, close to strong dislike.

clue.text: Unwelcome guest is, in time, less polite

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
ruder is the comparative of rude

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher who becomes more ill-mannered as the evening goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In time' looks like a phrase meaning eventually; the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is someone who enters a place where they are not wanted or invited.

clue.text: Jazz up weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: trad is short for traditional jazz

explanation.surface: An instruction to liven up a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jazz up' reads as one phrasal verb meaning enliven; it splits into the music style and the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dart is a small pointed missile thrown or shot as a weapon, as well as in the pub game.

clue.text: Cutting off end of piece and unravelling yarn in two parts

indicators.note: cutting off the end removes the last letter of the word that follows
unravelling undoes something's order, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a bit is a piece
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Snipping a length of wool and unpicking it into two strands.
explanation.definitionFit: Binary describes something composed of two elements, like a number system using only two digits.

clue.text: Note the listener's mood

indicators.note: what the listener hears is the sound of a word, not its spelling

blocks.note: the tenor of something is its general mood or drift

explanation.surface: Remark on how the audience is feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a verb meaning observe; it is a banknote. A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the everyday British name for a ten-pound banknote, so it is a kind of note.

clue.text: Real me is free to be less generous

indicators.note: letters set free are loosened from their order and can be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says that their true self, once liberated, would be stingier.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly means meagre or stingy, so the comparative form describes someone giving smaller amounts.
